messages:
Maya: Starting a thread to align on the Reserved Pools PRD acceptance criteria and edge cases for launch. I pushed a short PRD draft here: https://redwood.internal/prds/reserved-pools-draft (comments welcome).
Alex: Skimmed it — looks good overall. We need to firm SLA targets though. Customer asks are 99.9% p99 latency under surge, right?
Priya: For enterprise customers asking for reserved capacity, they expect predictable p95 and p99. Let's define target tiers: Gold: p95<200ms p99<350ms, Silver: p95<350ms p99<600ms.
John: Agree on tiers. Also include throughput guarantees: e.g., commit size maps to sustained RPS. Proposal in PRD: 1x commit = 100 rps sustained, 3x = 300 rps, burstability up to 3x for short windows.
Sophie: How long is a "short window"? customers will test bursts. We should specify burst window and cooldown.
Maya: Proposal: burst allowance = 2x sustained for 2 minutes, then a 10-minute cooldown with tokens replenishing linearly. Add to acceptance criteria.
Alex: Autoscaling requirements: Dedicated pools should scale horizontally within the tenant's pool only, not mix with other customers. Add autoscale SLO: scale up within 60s for 1 GPU equiv increments when queue depth exceeds threshold.
Priya: Also need graceful degradation policy: when capacity exhausted, fall back to hosted model variants with documented latency delta and cost implications. Add automatic and manual fallback modes.
John: Edge case: KV cache warming on a scale-up — first few requests may suffer p99 spikes. Acceptance criteria should permit one-off cold-start p99 spikes during scale events, but require metrics to show recovery within N tokens/requests.
Sophie: Suggest: allow p99 to breach target for up to 30s after a scale event, but median should remain stable. We need explicit test plans.
Maya: Test plan snippet I added to PRD:
```
- Load test scenarios: steady, ramp, sustained burst, multi-tenant noisy neighbor
- Measure p50/p95/p99, error rate, CPU/GPU util, queue length
- Failure injection: simulate lost nodes, slow network, cold KV cache
- Canary rollouts: 5% -> 25% -> 100% with health gates
```
Alex: Acceptance gates for rollout: health=green (error < 0.1%), p95 within tier target, no unexplained increase in request failures. Rollback threshold: error >0.5% or p99 > 2x target for >5min.
Priya: Who signs off on SLA wording and customer-facing doc? Recommend Product + SRE + Legal. Add a checklist in PRD for signoffs.
Maya: Will do. Also adding "pricing delta for reserved pools" section: need finance to confirm the unit economics mapping commit->price.
John: Ops question: how do we map commits to underlying GPU types? Some customers want specific hardware. Add constraints: customers can pin GPU family; we expose equivalence classes (A100-80GB equiv, A10G equiv).
Sophie: Edge case: hardware mismatch during maintenance windows. If pinned hardware not available, system should offer 1) queue until match, 2) offer temporary variant with consent, 3) auto-refund if we can't meet commit SLA. Document preferred default = offer temporary variant with explicit latency delta and 2x credit.
Alex: Security/compliance: Reserved pools in Private must respect VPC routing and key management. Add mandatory audit log requirement for all dedicated requests.
Priya: Monitoring: add per-pool dashboards: token-level cost, per-model latency histograms, scaling events, failed fallbacks. Also add synthetic tests per customer every minute.
Maya: For acceptance criteria, let's enumerate final items:
- Defined tier targets (Gold/Silver) present
- Throughput mapping commit->rps documented
- Autoscale SLOs and cooldown behavior documented
- Fallback policies and degraded-mode behavior documented
- Test plan with load/failure/canary steps included
- Signoff checklist for Product/SRE/Legal/Finance
- Customer-facing SLA draft and opt-in flow present

Sophie: Sounds complete. A couple more edge cases:
- Partial pool eviction during hardware failure (some VMs die) -> ensure fair degradation across customers rather than starving a single tenant.
- Long-running KV cache eviction across restarts -> add cache-repopulate telemetry.

John: Ops runbook note: add quick commands for emergency capacity bump and manual failover. E.g.:
```
# emergency add
redwood infra reserve-pool add --tenant $TENANT --gpus 2 --expires 01h
```
Alex: infra-bot: please schedule a load test for the draft PRD next Tue 09:00 PT against a staging reserved pool.
infra-bot: Load test job queued: reserved-pools-prd-smoke 2024-04-23T16:00:00Z. Notifying infra-runner.
Priya: I'll own the test coordination. Maya, after tests we can iterate on the cold-start tolerances.
Maya: Thanks. I'll update the PRD with these tweaks and re-share for signoff. Leaving the doc in review state. :thumbsup:
